The mucosal surface exhibits areas of hemorrhage, inflammation, and localized tissue necrosis or ulceration. A thin probe or marker is placed across the airway lumen to highlight the anatomical site and extent of the lesion. These findings are characteristic of acute laryngotracheitis or severe necrotizing inflammation in the upper respiratory tract.
